definitions.explanation: Describes a position, area, or period where the people, stock, or defenses on hand are too few for what is needed. Used of staffing above all, but also of inventory and of weak points in a defense.

examples.japanese: {夜間|やかん}は{人手|ひとで}が{手|て}{薄|うす}になる。
{守|まも}りが{手|て}{薄|うす}な{右|みぎ}サイドを{攻|せ}めた。
examples.english: They attacked the thinly defended right side.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}は{担当者|たんとうしゃ}が{休|やす}みで{対応|たいおう}が{手|て}{薄|うす}になるため、{早|はや}めにご{連絡|れんらく}ください。
examples.english: Coverage will be thin over the New Year holidays while staff are away, so please contact us early.

notes:
USAGE:
Most often used predicatively with なる — {手|て}{薄|うす}になる (to become short-handed) — and attributively as {手|て}{薄|うす}な. It describes the situation, not the people: saying a section is {手|て}{薄|うす} is not a criticism of the staff there.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人手|ひとで}が{手|て}{薄|うす}になる: to become short of hands
- {警備|けいび}が{手|て}{薄|うす}だ: security is thin
- {在庫|ざいこ}が{手|て}{薄|うす}だ: stock is running low
- {手|て}{薄|うす}な{時間帯|じかんたい}: hours with thin coverage

OPPOSITE:
- {手厚|てあつ}い: generous, attentive — plentiful care or support, the natural antonym.
